analysis: The only changes in docs/architecture/inference.md are documentation-only: the 'Last updated' line (line 3) and the `stop` row in the request parameter table near base/head line 2126. The `stop` row now describes per-request ReasoningStopScope for Gemma 4 and <think> parsers, which exclude reasoning and tool-call spans from stop-string matching. The native block engine matches the whole output. No source code, key handling, attestation, coordinator-provider protocol, cache storage, or authorization behavior changes in this PR, so I identified no concrete security regression. The supplied units (base 5337-5436 and head 1-419) are unchanged surrounding text apart from those two lines. I did not see the stop-handling implementation (`ReasoningStopScope`, `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift`), so I cannot verify that the described behavior matches the code. Possible security-relevant effects of that behavior, none of which this PR evidences: stop-string non-matching inside reasoning or tool spans could affect output bounding (T-010 GPU/memory consumption) or the visibility of withheld reasoning. Those would be implementation questions for a code PR, not a documentation finding. Threat model T-041 (prefix cache) and TB-007 are not affected by the diff. Residual uncertainty is low; this is a docs-only change.
